slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Partner with RouteSprout in 2027 instead of buying it on the proposed terms, and keep a staged, ARR-priced purchase that diligence must earn
The proposed $18M all-cash deal breaks the cash floor and pays back only on the sellers' assumptions
–	Price plus integration leaves $2M of cash, $7M below the floor
–	It covers its costs only if cross-sell reaches $2.3M, 96% of an unsigned plan
RouteSprout's customers are less stable than the pitch assumes, so integration must protect renewals
–	Logo churn rose from 12% to 21%, and 41 accounts hold 58% of ARR
–	A full migration uses the whole $4M integration cap, with 30% unscoped
Of the four paths, only the partnership meets the board's cash, timing and continuity tests in 2027
–	The staged deal clears the floor at signing, then falls below it within a year
–	The partnership costs a $1.2M minimum and delivers routing this summer
Keep buying as an option: run diligence alongside the partnership, then buy only on staged terms
–	Upfront cash must stay below about $8.4M, about 1.8 times ARR
–	The board decides at a Q4 2027 gate; if diligence fails, the partnership continues

The ceiling rests on four assumptions to test in diligence
▪	Integration stays at $3.5M; unscoped work lowers the ceiling dollar for dollar, and with a year of support it already reaches $4.35M against the $4M cap
▪	RouteSprout's loss stays at $1M a year (including founders' salaries), with no savings and no first-year cross-sell
▪	At the ceiling cash sits on the floor after a year, so the $7M earnout must be funded by the business itself
▪	The ceiling is about 1.8 times recognized ARR, compared with 2.3 times for the $11M staged offer
